THE LOCAL MEANING

What it is.

A Central Pacific Costa Rica offshore format focused on blue marlin near fish aggregating devices or seamount grounds. Quepos provides the existing departure profile. A FAD trip can require a multi-day boat plan; it should not be treated as a normal short coastal outing.

How it is fished.

Troll or pitch bait around offshore fish aggregating devices.

The research describes trolling or pitching bait around the offshore grounds. Ask the operator about the actual range, access, transit time, and overnight arrangement. Mid-spring through mid-fall is the cited magazine context. It does not establish current access to a particular device or private offshore installation.

Planning format: Multi-day; offshore sport-fishing boat. Confirm the actual duration with the provider.

EDITORIAL PREPARATION ADVICE

What to bring.

  • Offshore layers, sun protection, and secure deck footwear.
  • A small overnight bag for the agreed multi-day format.
  • Personal fishing gear only after the skipper confirms the billfish system and storage limits.

Before you go.

Can any Quepos day charter reach the FAD grounds?

Do not assume it can. Confirm range, travel time, access, and trip length with the actual vessel. This research describes a specialist multi-day format.

What seasonal window does the evidence support?

Mid-spring through mid-fall in the cited magazine account. A seasonal account does not confirm current availability. Use the linked authority for current rules.

What must I confirm before I book this trip?

Confirm the boat’s range, planned grounds, and permission to use the intended area. Ask about bait, complete tackle, meals, bunks, and crew rotation. Agree on an alternative if the vessel cannot reach the FAD grounds. Castward has no confirmed guide inventory for this trip type.
